specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:8:Audit history: Implementation reconciliation (2026-08-24, commit `2a27f5679bf6eb5ebec6371e75870be8fc9ada1b`). Earlier skeleton text that said `pool_id` was absent is stale: current merged code has default-off pool authority threading, manifest crypto primitives, route isolation, labeled route snapshots, SPEC-043 creator-onboarding surfaces, buyer/public policy/status documents, an MVP retention-policy registry, local route-time model-allowlist enforcement, authorized route-time `pool_policy_stale` failure when the routeable/policy freshness snapshot expires, provider-side positive pool-capability advertisement/gating for pool-selected traffic, manifest-derived settlement-mode projection with closed-vocabulary validation and local route/dispatch-time observe-vs-enforce fail-closed gating, signed emergency restrictive lifecycle controls for `paused`/`draining`/`retired`, signed provider-bound `revoke_immediate` controls that append durable revocation, bump the route-generation fence, notify active provider-specific revocation watchers without polling, cancel active uncommitted dispatch attempts for the revoked provider, and preserve gateway no-charge/pass-through semantics for marker-proven no-prior-dispatch `pool_state_stale` while settling conservatively when a provider row may already have been credited or a prior provider-dispatched retry already occurred, and a default-off production activation gate that still rejects production-labeled promotion unless coordinator config supplies an allowed launch environment, signed-launch evidence digest, and matching root-custody disclosure hash. The buyer dispatch path now records provider-dispatched pool deliveries in the live trustpool registry, and local/signed `retired` lifecycle controls fail closed with `delivery_drain_pending` until that pool's delivery counter reaches zero. SPEC-042 now has a non-promoting signed journey-result path, a local buyer-server harness, and committed signed redacted evidence for the narrow Layer 2 MVP request-path requirements (R002/R005/R006/R010). This SPEC remains non-conformant for production until the unresolved SPEC-042 launch blockers close: production durable-store evidence for accepted-manifest projection/high-water behavior, remaining production fail-closed predicate evidence, SPEC-042-owned closed schemas/retention matrix promotion, production activation evidence/rollout proof, and five-lane audit at 0 Critical / 0 High / 0 Medium.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:38:    "rationale": "The pool control plane is a new authority domain (`pool-control-plane`). Current merged code contains substantial default-off pool plumbing and SPEC-043 creator-onboarding enablement, so this is no longer a zero-implementation skeleton. A SPEC-042-owned non-promoting signed journey-result path plus local buyer-server journey harness now exists for R002/R005/R006/R010, local restrictive lifecycle admin controls and signed emergency controls now pause/drain/retire pools fail-closed without creating a second activation path, signed provider-bound `revoke_immediate` controls now append durable revocation, advance the route-generation fence, notify active provider-specific revocation watchers without polling, cancel active uncommitted dispatch attempts for that provider, preserve gateway no-charge/pass-through semantics for marker-proven no-prior-dispatch `pool_state_stale`, and preserve settlement when a provider row may already have been credited or a prior provider-dispatched retry already occurred. The buyer dispatch path now records active pool deliveries in the live trustpool registry, local/signed `retired` lifecycle controls require that registry to prove delivery drain before committing retirement, authorized stale routeable snapshots now fail closed as retryable `pool_policy_stale` rather than generic availability, manifest-derived settlement mode now fails closed when a pool requires enforce while the coordinator's effective settlement mode is observe with a dispatch-boundary recheck to cover hot reloads, and production-labeled promotion is default-blocked unless `trusted_pools.production_activation` supplies an allowed launch environment, signed-launch evidence digest, and matching root-custody disclosure hash. The promotion path can reactivate paused candidate pools only after rerunning local activation preflight, model allowlists are locally enforced at route time from the signed manifest-derived pool snapshot, and selected pool providers must positively advertise `trusted_pool_v1` before pool traffic can dispatch to them. Signed Layer 2 request-path evidence is committed for R002/R005/R006/R010, but it is intentionally evidence-only and does not promote full requirement conformance. SPEC-042 is partial and still not-deployed until accepted-manifest projection is audited in production migration evidence, production predicate evidence closes, SPEC-042-owned closed schemas/retention matrix promotion closes, production activation evidence/rollout proof exists, and the launch audit reaches 0 Critical / 0 High / 0 Medium. This is a Layer 2 (administrative trust) contract; it does NOT define cryptographic privacy, which is owned by SPEC-041 and future Layer 3 SPECs."
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:47:The product tier defined here is administrative trust, not cryptographic privacy. The single canonical product name is **"Trusted Pool"**; "MacProvider Subnet" and "Controlled Pool" are retired synonyms and MUST NOT be used in buyer-facing copy ("Subnet" additionally imports Bittensor validator/miner-incentive connotations that would mislead the crypto-adjacent audience). The term "Privacy Pool" is reserved for the Layer 3 capability set (SPEC-041 relay-blind request encryption and later unlinkability/anonymous-membership SPECs) and MUST NOT be applied to any capability defined solely by SPEC-042.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:77:SPEC-002 owns coordinator admission and routing. SPEC-042 adds a `pool_id` routing namespace and pool-scoped eligibility predicates, but MUST NOT bypass the SPEC-002 request lifecycle, provider assignment, capacity accounting, cancellation, or request-log ownership. Global (poolless) routing MUST continue to behave exactly as today when no `pool_id` is present, and global traffic MUST remain outside pool authorization and MUST NEVER serve as fallback for a request that selected a pool. *(Open-A is a representation-only decision — nullable `pool_id` vs. a reserved sentinel value on the wire/storage — and MUST NOT reopen whether global traffic is semantically a pool.)*
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:85:SPEC-006 owns the buyer API error envelope and OpenAI-compatible route shape. SPEC-042 adds a pool-selection mechanism and pool disclosure/error fields, but MUST preserve existing global behavior when no pool is selected, and MUST NOT expose stable provider IDs unless SPEC-006 is amended.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:106:| `pool_id` | Stable, mandatory authority identifier for a pool, derived as `base64url(SHA256(canonical identity core)[0:16])` (SPEC-042-R001). Stable for the pool's lifetime; ordinary policy/trust-predicate changes preserve it. |
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:128:- The **identity core** fixes the stable pool identity and MUST contain only identity-genesis fields: the pool's stable **root issuer** signing key id and a creator-chosen genesis nonce/parameters. It MUST NOT contain `pool_id`, `manifest_version`, any version-chaining hash, the rotating operational signer set, or any mutable/versioned policy field. `pool_id` MUST equal `base64url(SHA256(canonical length-prefixed identity core)[0:16])` and is therefore stable for the pool's lifetime. `pool_id` MUST NOT appear inside the identity-core digest preimage; it is carried alongside the signed manifest and MUST be rejected on mismatch against the recomputed identity-core digest. `pool_id` is a 128-bit truncation and is a **non-capability identifier** (a naming/grouping key for the membership ledger, blocklist, routing, logs, and settlement): authorization is never granted by presenting a `pool_id`, only by signature verification over the full identity/policy cores, which the coordinator recomputes. Second-preimage resistance is ~2^128; the only realistic truncation risk is an actor who controls two of its own pools colliding their ids (~2^64, limited blast radius), which the coordinator MUST still reject via full-core comparison. Operational admin/creator keys that sign policy cores and mutable fields are NOT in the identity core; they are a versioned signer set authorized by the root issuer (SPEC-042-R012), so rotating them preserves `pool_id`.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:131:The coordinator MUST reject manifests that are malformed, unsigned, signature-invalid (against the signer set in force per SPEC-042-R012), schema-invalid, `pool_id`-mismatched against the recomputed identity-core digest, non-monotonic in `manifest_version`, or broken in the `prev_manifest_core_hash` chain. A signed policy core whose `manifest_version` is less than or equal to the last accepted version for that stable `pool_id` MUST be rejected as a rollback. Mutable operational fields (e.g. disclosure wording, non-narrowing capacity hints) MUST be separately signed by an authorized operational admin key (SPEC-042-R012) and MUST NOT alter `pool_id` or the `manifest_core_digest`.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:133:Loosening any confidentiality/attestation/settlement predicate is a trust-contract change: it MUST mint a new `manifest_version` under the same stable `pool_id` with `prev_manifest_core_hash` lineage, and MUST NOT silently apply to in-flight route reservations issued under the prior policy core. The coordinator MUST durably retain policy-core history sufficient to reconstruct which policy core was in force for any settled request. Because `pool_id` is derived from the identity core only, ordinary policy and trust-predicate changes preserve `pool_id`; buyer references, logs, settlement grouping, and rollback checks remain stable across versions.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:149:A provider MUST be explicitly admitted to a pool by that pool's creator/admin before it is eligible for the pool's traffic. Membership MUST be a pool-scoped credential bound to an authenticated SPEC-003 provider identity and MUST be distinct from network-global provisional/trusted admission; satisfying global admission MUST NOT imply pool membership. A pool member MAY, by default, concurrently serve global (poolless) traffic. Per-request routing prevents a pool request from being served by a non-member and prevents a global buyer from receiving pool response content; it does NOT by itself eliminate shared-provider cross-request side channels (KV/prefix-cache occupancy, capacity, timing) on a co-serving member — cross-request cache sharing is bounded instead by SPEC-008 account-scoped `conv:` key derivation, and a pool sensitive to co-tenant side channels MUST use the dedicated-supply option below. Whether a given pool forbids co-tenancy and offers dedicated supply is a manifest choice that MUST be disclosed in `pool_policy.json` (SPEC-042-R008), because a buyer's mental model of a "dedicated" pool depends on it.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:204:Enabling a non-default `privacy_mode` requires a coordinated SPEC-041 and SPEC-040 amendment (version bump), because SPEC-041 v0.1's closed request/reservation/AAD schema and SPEC-040's wallet semantic signature do not currently reserve pool fields. That amendment MUST reserve and bind `pool_id`, `manifest_version`, `manifest_core_digest`, and the pool generation / `pool_state_epoch_hash` (SPEC-042-R005) into the SPEC-041 route reservation, the SPEC-041 AEAD AAD/transcript, the SPEC-040 wallet semantic signature, the route snapshot, and settlement context. Until that amendment lands, a pool that declares a non-default `privacy_mode` MUST fail closed rather than route, and conversely a v0.1 relay-blind (SPEC-041) request MUST NOT be pool-scoped at all — its closed envelope cannot carry bound pool selection, so any pool intent would be an unbound out-of-band source and MUST be rejected — so no unbound pool→global path exists. This SPEC forward-declares the fields so the amendment is additive, not a re-architecture.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:214:SPEC-042 defines this minimal SPEC-006-compatible error taxonomy. Predicate-specific and existence-revealing codes MUST be returned only to a caller already authorized for the pool; unauthorized or unknown-pool callers MUST receive the generic `pool_unavailable` so error responses do not reveal private-pool existence, membership health, attestation posture, or capacity timing. To avoid a timing oracle, the credential-scope check (is `pool_id` in the caller's authorized set?) MUST precede and be independent of any pool-registry existence or predicate evaluation, and the response latency for an unauthorized caller MUST NOT depend on whether the named pool exists.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:221:| `pool_at_capacity` | 503 | yes | authorized only | Eligible members exist but all are at capacity; fail-closed, no spill. Retry after backpressure. |
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:239:- closure of the open decisions: **Open-A** (nullable `pool_id` vs. reserved sentinel — representation only), **Open-B** (SPEC-015 signed-receipt field vs. route-snapshot context); the exact canonical **identity-core and versioned-policy-core** field encodings with golden test vectors are **CLOSED** (v0.0.8, `phase4-coordinator/internal/poolmanifest` + golden vectors), **policy-core signature verification** (M-of-N over a signer set, the signing preimage, and the `pool_id`-binding check) is **CLOSED** (v0.0.9, `phase4-coordinator/internal/poolmanifest/signature.go` + golden signature vectors), and per-requirement CONFORMANCE records for R001–R012 are **CLOSED** (registered in CONFORMANCE.json); **authority-log entry encoding + M-of-N chain verification** (versioned signer sets, hash chain, rollback/threshold checks, revocation, and signer-set materialization for policy-core verification) is **CLOSED** (v0.0.10, `phase4-coordinator/internal/poolmanifest/authoritylog.go` + golden vectors); **active-policy selection** (versioned policy-core history: signature verification against the authority-log signer sets, `pool_id` binding, monotonic `manifest_version`/rollback reject, `prev_manifest_core_hash` chain, non-overlapping half-open validity windows, and `pool_policy_stale` fail-closed selection) is **CLOSED** (v0.0.11, `phase4-coordinator/internal/poolmanifest/policyhistory.go` + vectors); **durable persistence + verdict-replay reconstruction** of the authority log + policy-core history + acceptance verdicts (the reversible snapshot codec and `ReconstructPool` that grandfathers a policy accepted before its signer set was later revoked) is **CLOSED** (v0.0.12, `phase4-coordinator/internal/poolmanifest/persist.go` + vectors); SPEC-043 now provides MVP policy/status document and retention-policy-registry evidence, but SPEC-042-owned promotion still requires closed JSON schema artifacts, the production retention matrix, and explicit acceptance that those SPEC-043 surfaces satisfy R007/R008 rather than merely enabling the creator-onboarding profile;
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:264:Migrating an existing global provider into a pool MUST require explicit creator member admission (SPEC-042-R003); a provider MUST NOT be auto-enrolled into a pool by virtue of global network membership. A pool MUST enforce the signed `min_eligible_members` supply-readiness threshold (SPEC-042-R001) below which `pool_status.json` reports non-`ready` and required traffic fails closed with `pool_no_eligible_member` rather than serving from insufficient or again-global supply. For a deterministic count, an **eligible member** is a current, non-revoked pool member that, at the route-time snapshot, passes all manifest predicates (SPEC-042-R004) and has fresh health within the SPEC-042-R003 freshness bound; members that are unhealthy, stale, or predicate-failing MUST NOT be counted. Whether a busy/at-capacity member counts toward `min_eligible_members` MUST be fixed by the manifest's readiness policy (default: capacity-blocked members count toward supply readiness but cannot receive a dispatch until a slot frees); the count MUST be taken from a single consistent snapshot, not summed across attempts. Because a member may be predicate-eligible yet saturated (especially under the co-tenancy default of SPEC-042-R003), `readiness = ready` MUST NOT be read as a promise of immediate free capacity. When every eligible member is at capacity, the request MUST NOT report `pool_no_eligible_member` (the members do satisfy predicates); it MUST either queue under existing SPEC-002 capacity backpressure or fail with the distinct typed error `pool_at_capacity` (SPEC-042-R010), never spill to global.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:282:Operational key rotation, threshold change, and compromised-key revocation MUST be expressed as new signer-set versions and MUST preserve `pool_id` (they do not touch the identity core). Root-issuer compromise or loss has **no in-pool recovery**: it MUST require minting a new pool (new identity core -> new `pool_id`) with signed `supersedes` lineage to the retired `pool_id`, and buyers MUST be able to follow that lineage. An authorized signer set (or the root issuer) MUST be able to trigger an emergency `paused`/`draining`/`revoke_immediate` transition (SPEC-042-R011/R003) via a signed control message that the coordinator honors fail-closed. The signed control path now covers `paused`/`draining`/`retired`, `retired` requires the live delivery-drain proof from R011, and `revoke_immediate` now creates a provider-specific durable revocation record, advances the route-generation fence, and cancels active uncommitted dispatch attempts for that provider. The authority log and current signer set MUST be durable and reconstructable across restart/failover (SPEC-042-R011).
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:284:**Authority-log entry encoding and chain verification.** Each authority-log entry has a canonically-encoded, domain-separated **content** (the hashed, chained part) plus the authorizing **signatures** (not hashed). The content grammar uses the same length-prefixed framing (SPEC-041-R002 precedent) under the fixed ASCII domain tag `macprovider/spec042/authority-log-entry/v1`, encoding in order: `pool_id` (binding the entry to its pool so it cannot be replayed into another pool's log — the log is keyed under `pool_id`), `signer_set_version` (`>= 1`; version 0 is reserved as the root-authorizer sentinel), `prev_authority_log_entry_hash` (32 bytes; genesis = 32 zero bytes), the signer key set (`key_id` + Ed25519 `public_key`, byte-lexicographically ordered by `key_id`, no duplicate id and no duplicate public key), the threshold `M`, the validity window (`not_before_unix`, `expires_at_unix`), the strictly-ascending, distinct `revokes_versions` list (rejected, not normalized, if out of order or duplicated), and `authorizing_signer_set_version` (0 = root issuer). `authority_log_entry_hash = SHA256(content)`; authorizers sign the domain-separated message `macprovider/spec042/authority-log-entry-sig/v1 ‖ authority_log_entry_hash` (a distinct signing tag so an authority-log signature can never be replayed as a policy-core signature). Replaying a log verifies, per entry: the established set is structurally valid (`1 ≤ M ≤ N`, distinct keys); `signer_set_version` strictly increases (rollback rejected); the prev-hash chain is intact; each `revokes_versions` entry is a prior existing version; and the entry is authorized either by exactly one root-issuer signature (`authorizing_signer_set_version = 0`) or by `M`-of-`N` of a prior, still-authorized (unrevoked, window-containing the entry's `not_before_unix`), lower-versioned signer set — with the authorization checked before the entry's own revocations apply, so a set may authorize its own replacement then be revoked. Replay binds the log to the pool identity (the supplied root-issuer key must match the identity core's `root_issuer_key_id`, and every entry's `pool_id` must equal the identity core's derived `pool_id`) and materializes `signer_set_version → SignerSet` (with revocation state, deep-copied so the verified signer material cannot be mutated through the caller's inputs) — the exact value policy-core verification consumes. This is implemented in `phase4-coordinator/internal/poolmanifest/authoritylog.go` and frozen by golden vectors in `authoritylog_test.go`. The durable snapshot codec and verdict-replay **reconstruction** of the authority log + policy-core history + acceptance verdicts are implemented in slice 5 (`persist.go`, see the R011 reconstruction note); v0.0.15 locally wires accepted-manifest projection/high-water evidence into the coordinator store, while full authority-log snapshot persistence and highest-accepted signer-set rollback proof remain pending.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:307:- 0.0.28 - Added a default-off production activation gate for Trusted Pool promotion. `trusted_pools.production_activation` now requires an explicit allowed non-candidate launch environment, signed-launch evidence SHA-256 digest, and root-custody disclosure hash allowlist before a production-labeled root issuer can promote to active; absent or mismatched configuration preserves the prior fail-closed `launch_environment_not_candidate`/production precondition behavior. Coordinator startup passes the configured gate into the durable store, examples document the default-blocked YAML surface, and regression coverage proves partial config rejection, custody mismatch rejection, and matching evidence/custody activation. No requirement is promoted: signed journey artifacts, production migration/predicate evidence, SPEC-042-owned closed schemas/retention matrix promotion, rollout proof, and 0 C/H/M launch audit remain required.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:309:- 0.0.26 - Added authorized route-time `pool_policy_stale` handling for expired routeable/policy freshness snapshots. `trustpool.Snapshot` now carries `RouteableExpired` from the same locked read that computes routeability and generation, durable routeable-snapshot refresh preserves creator-agreement expiry as that same bit after materializing the pool as non-routeable, and pool-selected routing returns retryable `pool_policy_stale` only after authorization succeeds and the existing pool's routeable snapshot has expired; unknown, unauthorized, disabled, or non-active pools still collapse to non-disclosing `pool_unavailable`. Added coordinator regression coverage and explicit retryability/error-code registration. No requirement is promoted: signed journey evidence, production activation/migration evidence, remaining production predicate evidence, and 0 C/H/M launch audit remain required.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:316:- 0.0.19 - Added local fail-closed route-time enforcement for the signed manifest model allowlist. Durable replay now projects `PolicyCore.ModelAllowlist` into routeable snapshots, the hot registry snapshots/export/import preserve the allowlist with generation fencing, and buyer routing rejects selected-pool requests whose requested model is outside the pool allowlist with non-retryable `pool_model_not_allowed` (400) before any global fallback. Pinned provider/session routes and slot-queue candidate/poll paths re-check the same snapshot verdict, including a conservative model-class rule: a class alias is allowed only when every concrete member of the resolved class is allowlisted. Buyer policy/status documents now expose `model_allowlist`. No requirement is promoted: signed journey evidence, production activation evidence, remaining predicate/status freshness blockers, signed emergency lifecycle controls, and 0 C/H/M launch audit remain required.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:319:- 0.0.16 - Added a dedicated local restrictive lifecycle admin endpoint, `POST /admin/trust-pools/pools/{pool_id}/lifecycle`, for fail-closed `paused`/`draining`/`retired` transitions. The endpoint reuses the validated durable append path, refreshes routeable snapshots after commit, preserves buyer allowlist metadata while removing routeable members from paused/draining/retired pools, treats invalid lifecycle transitions as fail-closed registry-clearing malformed input, and rejects `active` with `activation_requires_promotion` so `promote` remains the only routeability-increasing path. No requirement is promoted: this is operator-token local admin control, not R012 signed emergency lifecycle messages; signed journey evidence, production migration evidence, full delegation/lifecycle reconstruction, and launch audit remain blockers.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:325:- 0.0.10 - R012 implementation slice 3 (authority log): implemented the append-only, hash-chained **authority log** that establishes and versions the operational **signer sets** policy-core verification (slice 2) consumes. Defined the authority-log-entry content byte grammar (domain tag `macprovider/spec042/authority-log-entry/v1`) + `authority_log_entry_hash` + the distinct entry signing preimage, and the chain-replay verifier `BuildAuthorityLog(rootIssuer, entries)`: per-entry signer-set structural validation, strictly-monotonic `signer_set_version` (rollback rejected), prev-hash chain, `revokes_versions` (prior-existing only), and authorization by either one root-issuer signature or `M`-of-`N` of a prior still-authorized (unrevoked, window-containing) lower-versioned set — authorization evaluated before the entry's own revocations, enabling rotate-and-revoke. Replay materializes `signer_set_version → SignerSet` with revocation state. Extracted a shared `verifyThresholdMessage` primitive (policy-core verification byte-identical). Lives in `phase4-coordinator/internal/poolmanifest/authoritylog.go`, frozen by golden vectors (genesis → rotate → revoke). Binds each entry to its pool (`pool_id` in the content) and to the identity core's root issuer so a log signed under a reused root key cannot be replayed into another pool; reserves `signer_set_version = 0`; rejects non-ascending `revokes_versions`; and deep-copies materialized signer material. Closes the last deferred R001/R012 canonical-encoding deliverable. Pure (no I/O/persistence/wall-clock); durable persistence + restart reconstruction + the acceptance-verdict record remain a later slice. Default-inert.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:328:- 0.0.7 - Round 5 re-audit: BOTH subagent lanes PASS at 0 Critical / 0 High / 0 Medium (product-design critic PASS C:0/H:0/M:0/L:1/I:2; adversarial verifier PASS C:0/H:0/M:0/L:3/I:2, mechanisms verified composable, no regressions). The five-lane promotion gate (code/security/architecture via codex + product-design/adversarial via subagents) is complete at 0 C/H/M. Closed the carried LOW/INFO for polish: relabeled `pool_status.json` coordinator-attested in Terms/§1 (was "buyer-verifiable"); scoped the co-tenancy claim to per-request routing + SPEC-008 `conv:` cache bounding, directing side-channel-sensitive pools to dedicated supply (R003); required a single consistent (membership, generation) capture to preclude TOCTOU (R003); made claim-control machine-enforced — coordinator rejects a signed `confidentiality_scope` overclaim at acceptance (R009); defined the saturated-but-eligible outcome with a distinct `pool_at_capacity` code and clarified `ready` is not a free-capacity promise (R011/R010); retired the last "subnet" synonym in §1. Remaining items are INFO only.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:332:- 0.0.3 - Round 2 audit applied (code C:0/H:1/M:4/L:1, security C:0/H:0/M:5/L:1/I:1, architect C:0/H:1/M:1/L:2/I:1). Fixed the shared High by splitting stable pool identity (`pool_id` = digest of an identity/genesis core) from the versioned policy core (`manifest_core_digest`, `manifest_version`, `prev_manifest_core_hash`) so policy changes preserve `pool_id` (R001). Made attestation tiers an ordered lattice where hardware satisfies an `se_custody` minimum, and required coordinator-held SPEC-020 release evidence for the binary-version predicate (R004). Made revocation synchronously bump pool generation, invalidate un-dispatched reservations, and fail closed on unknown freshness (R003). Narrowed settlement to labels-only and deferred creator-split execution to a SPEC-005/SPEC-016-amended V1 (R006); added SPEC-016 dependency. Added a credential-header retention denylist (R007). Reframed Layer 3 privacy binding as blocked-until-SPEC-041/040-amended and added pool generation/epoch to the binding set (R009). Restricted `pool_selection_invalid` to syntactic conflicts so it cannot leak pool existence (R010). Added a deterministic lifecycle transition table (R011). Reframed Open-A as representation-only. Status `draft-skeleton`→`draft` with a `Maturity: skeleton` note for registry legibility. AUTHORITY consumer edges added for consumed domains.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:59:SPEC-001 remains authoritative for the `macprovider-cli` binary lifecycle, provider-binary packaging conventions, and existing provider-side inference-server behavior. SPEC-045 consumes that CLI authority only to reserve and define the new `consume` subcommand contract for buyer-side local endpoint mode; it does not change SPEC-001's provider wire protocol or provider serving path.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:61:SPEC-006 remains authoritative for the public buyer gateway's OpenAI-compatible request/response surface, upstream authentication, quota enforcement, and error semantics. SPEC-045 may proxy only the SPEC-006-compatible endpoints it implements locally, and it must preserve upstream gateway enforcement rather than replacing it.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:102:- Pricing admission fails closed unless trusted signed pricing is fresh enough or an explicit unpriced override can reserve the full remaining budget without violating per-request caps.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:103:- Upstream gateway errors are preserved to the initiating local client, but other diagnostics receive only redacted code/class/request-id material.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:115:**SPEC-045-R001 - Loopback-only local command.** `macprovider-cli` MUST expose a local consumer endpoint command, with a stable spelling reserved for `consume`, that starts a plain HTTP/1.1 server bound to a loopback interface. The default bind address MUST be `127.0.0.1`; IPv6 loopback `::1` MAY be supported. The default port MUST be `11435`; port `0`, port collision, bind failure, or rejected bind input MUST fail startup with a nonzero exit and a redacted stderr error code `local_bind_rejected` rather than silently selecting a different port. Bind validation MUST be allowlist-based: after address parsing and name resolution, the only accepted listener addresses are IPv4 loopback addresses in `127.0.0.0/8` and IPv6 `::1`. If the implementation accepts the hostname `localhost` as a bind input, it MUST normalize it to an accepted loopback literal before binding, MUST prefer `127.0.0.1` when both IPv4 and IPv6 loopback records are available and IPv6 loopback was not explicitly requested, and MUST NOT reject it solely because IPv6 loopback is unsupported. The command MUST reject wildcard, LAN, VPN, public, Unix-domain, hostname-resolved non-loopback, or interface-scoped listener exposure unless a later spec defines an authenticated multi-user mode. The command MUST print the local base URL, upstream gateway origin, active model allowlist summary, budget mode, unpriced-request override state, and credential-source class on startup. Startup status information MUST be written to stderr; structured machine-readable output, when explicitly requested by a later flag or command, MUST be written to stdout. The model allowlist summary MUST print the total count and, when non-empty, a sample of up to five model ids; an empty allowlist MUST print an explicit empty-allowlist warning. It MUST NOT print the upstream bearer token, an expanded absolute credential path, a home-directory path, a username-bearing path, a secret-bearing path component, or any client prompt/completion content.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:117:**SPEC-045-R002 - OpenAI-compatible endpoint subset.** The accepted local path set for v0.1 is `GET /v1/models`, `POST /v1/chat/completions`, and `GET /v1/status` as defined by R006; the local server MUST implement those paths before the mode can be promoted beyond draft. `GET /v1/status` is a local diagnostic carve-out, not the public SPEC-006 gateway status surface, and MUST NOT be proxied upstream. Before local authentication, the server MUST enforce bounded HTTP request-line bytes, bounded request-target bytes, bounded percent-decoding/parser work for the request target, bounded HTTP header bytes, bounded header count, a bounded header-read deadline, and a bounded cap on incomplete/pre-auth connections; violations MUST close or reject the request without body buffering or upstream forwarding. Requests with a non-empty local query string MUST fail locally as `local_invalid_request` and MUST NOT be forwarded, logged, or preserved as endpoint identity in status or diagnostics. After local auth succeeds under R003 and before endpoint matching for every local path, it MUST normalize the HTTP request path by resolving percent-encoding, MUST reject malformed encodings, encoded slash/backslash path separators, raw or encoded dot-segment components, and any path whose normalized form is not an exact supported path, and MUST NOT construct an upstream URL from an unnormalized local path. Requests with ambiguous framing, including duplicate `Content-Length`, conflicting `Content-Length`, any request containing both `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding`, unsupported `Transfer-Encoding`, stacked transfer codings, non-final transfer codings, or any transfer coding other than a single final `chunked` coding when chunked is accepted, MUST fail locally as `local_invalid_request` before body buffering. Requests with `Content-Encoding` other than absent or `identity` MUST fail locally as `local_content_encoding_unsupported` and MUST NOT be forwarded upstream. Chunked local request transfer encoding MAY be accepted, but when accepted it MUST be decoded before body-size enforcement, duplicate-key detection, budget estimation, and upstream forwarding; the upstream-forwarded original body bytes are the decoded entity body bytes, not the local wire-framing bytes. Request bodies MUST be bounded before buffering or budget estimation to the smallest applicable limit among a local hard ceiling of 100 MiB, the trusted upstream/SPEC-006 request-body cap when known, and a default 1 MiB cap when no trusted upstream cap is available; larger bodies MUST fail locally as `local_request_too_large` and MUST NOT be forwarded upstream. `GET /v1/models` MUST return only gateway models that are currently visible through the upstream buyer model surface and allowed by the local model filter. If no explicit local model allowlist is supplied, the default allowlist MUST be empty: `/v1/models` MUST return an OpenAI-compatible empty model-list response and MAY include `X-MacProvider-Warning: empty_model_allowlist`, while `/v1/chat/completions` MUST reject chargeable requests as `local_model_not_allowed` until the operator supplies at least one allowed model. `POST /v1/chat/completions` MUST accept OpenAI-compatible JSON and streaming requests for allowed models, forward all standard SPEC-006/OpenAI chat-completions request fields verbatim unless this spec or a later SPEC-045 version explicitly restricts a field, and preserve streaming chunk order and termination semantics from the upstream gateway. Before admission or forwarding, the local server MUST parse the bounded JSON body with duplicate-object-key detection and MUST reject any duplicate JSON object key anywhere in the request body as `local_invalid_request`; the implementation MUST NOT rely on last-key-wins, first-key-wins, or parser-specific duplicate-key behavior for admission-relevant fields. The request body forwarded upstream MUST be the decoded entity body bytes as received after local transfer decoding; parsing for budget estimation MUST operate on a separate read of the same bounded buffer and MUST NOT cause JSON reserialization, field reordering, whitespace normalization, or semantic rewriting of the body sent upstream. Tool-calling fields such as `tools`, `tool_choice`, assistant `tool_calls`, and tool-result messages MUST NOT be dropped or rewritten by the local proxy; if the upstream gateway rejects them, the upstream error must be preserved under R007. Unsupported local paths or methods MUST fail with an OpenAI-shaped error envelope and MUST NOT be forwarded opportunistically, except unsupported `HEAD` requests MUST return `405` with no response body. `/v1/responses`, embeddings, image, audio, batch, fine-tune, or provider-control paths are out of scope until a later SPEC-045 version names their proxy and budget rules.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:125:**SPEC-045-R003 - Upstream credential custody.** The command MUST obtain the upstream buyer credential from a bounded local source order: an explicit `--credential-file <path>` flag, `MACPROVIDER_HTTP2_API_KEY_FILE`, the default user-owned credential file `~/.config/macprovider/buyer-api-key`, `MACPROVIDER_HTTP2_API_KEY`, `MP_API_KEY`, then `BUYER_TOKEN`. The ordering is intentional: explicit credential-file sources, including `MACPROVIDER_HTTP2_API_KEY_FILE`, override the default durable user-owned MacProvider credential file; the default file takes precedence over raw-key environment variables. Credential-source class values MUST be the closed enum `explicit_file`, `default_config_file`, `environment`, or `missing`; `MACPROVIDER_HTTP2_API_KEY_FILE` uses class `explicit_file`, while `MACPROVIDER_HTTP2_API_KEY`, `MP_API_KEY`, and `BUYER_TOKEN` use class `environment`. Raw API keys MUST NOT be accepted as command-line flag values; a raw-key flag attempt MUST fail startup with a nonzero exit and redacted stderr error code `local_credential_flag_rejected`. The configured upstream gateway URL MUST default to the MacProvider production gateway origin, MUST use the `https` scheme, MUST pass normal platform TLS certificate and hostname verification, MUST reject expired certificates, untrusted roots, invalid chains, and hostname mismatches, MUST NOT contain a username or password component, path other than empty or `/`, query, or fragment, and MUST resolve only to globally routable addresses. Implementations MUST treat the configured upstream as an origin only (`scheme`, `host`, and optional `port`) for request construction and status output; any operator input with path, query, or fragment MUST fail startup as `local_upstream_url_rejected` rather than being preserved or joined with local paths. Startup and each new upstream connection MUST reject loopback, link-local, wildcard, multicast, private, carrier-grade NAT, documentation, reserved, IPv6 unique-local, IPv6 special-purpose, IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses under `::ffff:0:0/96` whose embedded IPv4 address is non-global, and any other non-global address range; implementations MUST unwrap IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses and apply all IPv4 block checks to the embedded IPv4 address before accepting the upstream address; rejected upstream URL input MUST fail startup with redacted stderr error code `local_upstream_url_rejected`, and a post-startup DNS validation failure MUST fail closed as `local_upstream_unavailable` without sending the buyer credential. The upstream transport MUST disable environment proxy, redirect, and connection-rewrite bypasses for gateway requests unless a later spec authorizes them, and MUST either connect to a previously validated global address or verify that the actual connected peer address remains in the validated global-address set before sending upstream `Authorization`. Credential files MUST be opened with user-only permissions or fail closed with a remediation message that names the credential-source class, observed permission class, and required permission class without printing the expanded path or token. File-based credential paths MUST be current-user-owned, MUST NOT resolve through parent directories writable by other users, MUST NOT be symlink-ambiguous when the R005 symlink-ambiguity rule is applied to the credential file path and credential parent directories, and MUST be revalidated before accepting a metadata-triggered reload. File credential initial load and reload MUST open the credential with no-follow semantics, then verify ownership, permissions, and file identity on the already-open file descriptor before accepting the bytes; a second path-only stat after opening is not sufficient. The local server MUST use the stored upstream credential for gateway authorization and MUST construct upstream request headers from implementation-owned metadata plus the decoded local request body bytes required by R002 rather than proxying arbitrary local client headers. Upstream redirects MUST NOT be followed automatically; syntactically valid upstream redirect responses MUST be returned to the initiating local client under R007 without sending the buyer credential to the redirect target, and `Location` MUST be stripped from those local responses because it is not in the R007 response-header allowlist. The implementation MUST generate upstream `Content-Type: application/json` for chat-completions requests, including streaming requests; it MUST NOT forward the local client's `Content-Type`. `Accept` MAY be forwarded only when its value is `application/json` or `text/event-stream`; any other local-client `Accept` value MUST be omitted or replaced by an implementation-owned value. All other upstream headers, including authorization, content length, user agent, gateway auth, tracing, and idempotency metadata, MUST be generated or omitted by the local implementation. The implementation MUST NOT forward local-client `Authorization`, `api-key`, `x-api-key`, cookie, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Proxy-Connection`, `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Port`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, `X-Real-IP`, `Via`, `Connection`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Keep-Alive`, `Upgrade`, `Trailer`, `Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Sec-Fetch-Mode`, `Sec-Fetch-Dest`, `Sec-Fetch-User`, or `Sec-Purpose` headers upstream. At startup the server MUST generate a per-run local bearer token from at least 128 bits of CSPRNG input, MUST require that token on every local HTTP request through either `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, `api-key: <token>`, or `x-api-key: <token>`, and MUST reject absent or mismatched local credentials as `local_auth_required` before path normalization, body buffering, duplicate-key parsing, budget estimation, path-specific admission, or forwarding. The local bearer token MUST be written only to startup/setup output and the user-private active endpoint descriptor required by R006, MUST be redacted from logs, status, ledger rows, diagnostics, errors, and upstream requests, MUST be ignored for upstream identity, and MUST expire when the process exits. User-facing examples SHOULD use the generated local token as the OpenAI SDK `api_key` value rather than an empty string or the upstream buyer credential. Because local client authorization is not upstream identity, the server MUST keep browser-origin access default-deny: it MUST NOT emit permissive CORS headers, MUST reject CORS preflight requests, MUST unconditionally reject requests with `Origin: null`, MUST reject requests with any other `Origin` header value unless that value exactly equals the bound endpoint origin including scheme, the actual bound host literal, and port, for example `http://127.0.0.1:<bound-port>`, `http://127.0.0.2:<bound-port>` when explicitly bound to `127.0.0.2`, or `http://[::1]:<bound-port>`, MUST evaluate exact-origin comparison per listener when both IPv4 and IPv6 loopback listeners are enabled, MUST inspect browser fetch metadata before stripping it from any upstream-bound request, MUST reject browser fetch metadata that identifies a cross-site or cross-origin caller, and MUST NOT add a browser-access allowlist unless a later spec defines cross-origin delegation. When an upstream authentication failure indicates the stored buyer credential is invalid or expired, the server MUST keep running, mark local credential state as `invalid_or_expired` in status, return the upstream auth failure under R007, and re-read a file-based credential before the next request when file metadata shows an inode number, file size, ctime, mtime, or symlink target change. If a previously loaded file credential is deleted, becomes unreadable, or fails ownership, permission, file-identity, or symlink revalidation, the implementation MUST immediately zeroize and discard the cached upstream credential, status MUST report credential state `missing` before the next request, and chargeable requests MUST fail before upstream connection or forwarding as `local_credential_missing` until a conforming credential is loaded again.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:133:**SPEC-045-R004 - Conservative model and exposure admission.** The command MUST support an explicit local model allowlist and a cumulative local estimated-exposure limit expressed in USD-equivalent units through `--budget-usd <amount>`. `--budget-usd` is a local admission cap and is not a buyer billing balance, settlement ledger, payment authorization, refund rule, or source of truth for gateway charges. `--budget-usd 0`, negative values, non-finite values, and unparsable values MUST fail startup with a nonzero exit and redacted stderr error code `local_budget_flag_rejected`; they MUST NOT be silently treated as an exhausted budget or as `--no-budget`. Before forwarding a chargeable request, the command MUST require either a positive `--budget-usd <amount>` or an explicit `--no-budget` risk acknowledgement for the process, MUST check that the requested model is allowed, that the model appears in trusted upstream/catalog metadata, and that the request can be admitted without exceeding the remaining local exposure cap under a conservative exposure estimate. Admission-relevant fields, including `model`, `messages`, `max_tokens`, output-bound fields, `stream`, tool-calling fields, and structured-output fields, MUST be read only from the duplicate-key-free parse required by R002; an explicit JSON `null` output bound MUST be treated as absent and estimated from the model's trusted maximum output limit. Trusted pricing metadata for v0.1 means either a SPEC-006 public `GET /v1/rate-card` body paired with `GET /v1/rate-card.sig` that verifies as Ed25519 against the SPEC-023 repo-trusted static catalog keyring and satisfies SPEC-023 detached-sidecar, policy-version, and `generated_at` freshness rules, or a gateway quote/estimate result only if that quote/estimate surface is defined by SPEC-006 or a later dependency. Missing or malformed sidecars, unknown or retired key ids, non-Ed25519 algorithms, invalid signatures, policy mismatch, projection-hash mismatch, future-dated bytes beyond the SPEC-023 tolerance, rate-card bytes older than the SPEC-023 maximum age, or a fetched rate card older than the baked trusted snapshot MUST fail closed as `local_pricing_unavailable` unless `--allow-unpriced` applies. A trusted rate card MUST use the catalog release shape validated by `scripts/catalog-release.py`: top-level `version`, `policy_version`, `generated_at`, `usd_per_million_credits`, and non-empty `rows` containing a `default` row, with each row carrying `prompt_rate_per_mtok`, `prompt_cache_hit_rate_per_mtok`, `completion_rate_per_mtok`, `provider_share_bps`, and `global_multiplier_ppm`; its `version` MUST equal the rate-card projection hash, and model-key lookup MUST follow SPEC-005 §5.5 exact, normalized, then default resolution. A gateway `/v1/models` result is trusted only for model visibility and model id presence, not for price or output-limit authority. If the trusted rate card or trusted quote surface cannot supply price fields for the requested model or default row, or if a request lacks an explicit output bound and no trusted maximum output bound is available, budgeted admission MUST fail as `local_pricing_unavailable` unless `--allow-unpriced` applies. Unsigned local files, client request fields, or ad hoc environment values are not trusted metadata. Trusted metadata MUST be fetched at startup or before first admission and MAY be refreshed only at bounded implementation-defined intervals; it MUST NOT run as an unbounded background refresh loop. Before every chargeable admission, cached trusted pricing metadata MUST be revalidated against the local clock and SPEC-023 freshness rules. If the cached metadata has crossed the SPEC-023 stale-warning boundary, status MUST surface `stale_pricing` in the pricing warning-code list required by R006 while admission MAY continue until the reject boundary. If it has crossed the SPEC-023 maximum-age or future-skew reject boundary, the pricing trust state MUST be atomically marked `unavailable`, new chargeable admission MUST fail as `local_pricing_unavailable` unless `--allow-unpriced` can produce a conforming conservative reservation under R004, and the implementation MUST NOT continue admitting from expired cached pricing. The admission check and reservation write MUST be atomic within the process so no two concurrent requests can both pass admission before either one reduces the remaining budget. The estimate MUST use trusted catalog/rate metadata and request bounds such as `max_tokens` when available; it MUST NOT trust client-supplied prices, client-supplied token counts, provider hints, or response metadata as the source of cost authority. The conservative admission estimate MUST be the gross buyer-side USD-equivalent exposure, never provider payout or provider-share exposure. Arithmetic MUST use fixed-point integer or exact rational math with overflow detection; overflow, precision loss, missing operands, non-finite values, or any under-reserving ambiguity MUST fail closed as `local_pricing_unavailable`. For v0.1, prompt cost MUST be estimated as `estimated_prompt_tokens * prompt_rate_per_mtok / 1_000_000` using the full `prompt_rate_per_mtok`; cached-token discounts from `prompt_cache_hit_rate_per_mtok` MUST NOT be applied unless a trusted gateway quote/estimate surface defined by SPEC-006 or a later dependency distinguishes trusted cache-hit token counts. Completion cost MUST be `bounded_completion_tokens * completion_rate_per_mtok / 1_000_000`. The sum MUST then apply `global_multiplier_ppm` multiplicatively as in SPEC-005 gross-credit math, converted through trusted `usd_per_million_credits` when credits-to-USD conversion is needed, and rounded upward to the smallest representable local ledger unit before reservation. `provider_share_bps` MUST NOT reduce the buyer exposure estimate. Prompt exposure MUST be estimated from the submitted request body using a trusted gateway estimate, a tokenizer bound to the requested model's trusted catalog identity, or a byte-to-token upper bound no less conservative than one UTF-8 byte equals one token. Completion exposure MUST use the request's explicit output bound when present; when no bound is present, it MUST use the model's trusted maximum output limit, and if that limit is unavailable budgeted mode MUST reject the request as `local_pricing_unavailable`. When trusted pricing is unavailable and a positive run budget is configured, the request MUST fail closed unless the operator supplied an explicit unpriced-request override for that run using `--allow-unpriced`. Under `--allow-unpriced` with a positive run budget, each unpriced chargeable request MUST reserve the entire remaining local budget before forwarding, ledger `admission estimate` MUST equal the pre-request remaining budget, status remaining budget MUST become zero until settlement/recovery changes it, concurrent unpriced chargeable admissions MUST fail as `local_budget_exceeded` while that reservation is active, and if trusted upstream usage/cost evidence remains unavailable at terminal settlement the reservation MUST settle to that full admission estimate. Any `--no-budget` or unpriced-request override MUST be shown at startup, included in local status, recorded in the ledger when a ledger is active, and surfaced as a warning before or with each affected chargeable request using response header `X-MacProvider-Warning` with value `no_budget` or `unpriced_override`; this warning header MUST NOT alter the OpenAI JSON or SSE body. If an upstream response already contains `X-MacProvider-Warning`, the local warning value MUST be appended as a distinct comma-separated token without deleting upstream warning values.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:135:R004 implementations MUST also support an optional per-request estimated-exposure cap through `--max-request-usd <amount>`. The flag uses the same USD-equivalent parsing rules as `--budget-usd`: zero, negative, non-finite, or unparsable values MUST fail startup with `local_budget_flag_rejected`. For every chargeable request, the same conservative admission estimate used for cumulative budget reservation MUST be computed before forwarding and MUST be less than or equal to the configured per-request cap. A request whose estimate exceeds the per-request cap MUST fail locally as `local_request_cap_exceeded`, MUST NOT create a budget reservation, MUST NOT append a ledger request row, and MUST NOT be forwarded upstream. `--max-request-usd` MAY be used with `--budget-usd` or `--no-budget`; when used with `--no-budget`, it remains a per-request safety rail even though cumulative budget configured/used/held/remaining are null. Under `--allow-unpriced`, the per-request cap MUST still apply to the unpriced reservation amount; if the entire remaining local budget would be reserved and that amount exceeds `--max-request-usd`, the request MUST fail as `local_request_cap_exceeded`.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:141:**SPEC-045-R005 - Restart-safe budget ledger.** When a cumulative run budget is configured, the command MUST persist a local exposure ledger under the default user-private state path `$HOME/Library/Application Support/macprovider/consume/ledgers/default.jsonl` on macOS unless the operator supplies an explicit ledger path, and it MUST hold an OS-enforced exclusive advisory file lock on a lock file named `<ledger-filename>.lock` adjacent to the ledger. The lock MUST use OS lock state, not lockfile presence; a stale lock file from a crashed process MUST NOT prevent a new process from acquiring the lock after the OS releases the prior lock on process termination. Ledger path class values MUST be the closed enum `default_user_state`, `explicit_absolute`, or `explicit_relative`; explicit relative ledger paths MUST resolve relative to the current working directory captured at process startup. The implementation MUST refuse any mode that creates a ledger, including budgeted mode and `--no-budget --ledger <path>`, when the state path is not user-private, is symlink-ambiguous, is not on a local filesystem with verified exclusive-lock semantics, or cannot be locked by exactly one active process. Implementations MUST verify local filesystem lock support using OS metadata such as `statfs`/`fstatfs` or a stronger platform-specific check, and MUST fail closed when the filesystem type or mount properties cannot be verified as local with real exclusive-lock semantics. A state path is symlink-ambiguous when the ledger path, lock path, or any parent directory resolves through a symlink that is not owned by the current OS user, or when the resolved target changes between validation and open/lock. Passing `--ledger <path>` without either `--budget-usd <amount>` or `--no-budget` MUST fail startup with `local_budget_flag_rejected` rather than creating an idle ledger whose admission mode is ambiguous. When `--no-budget` is combined with an explicit `--ledger <path>`, the ledger MUST be created, locked, and written with per-request no-budget records; the ledger path class is `explicit_absolute` or `explicit_relative` as appropriate. When `--no-budget` is used without an explicit `--ledger`, no ledger is created and per-request no-budget state is in-memory only. The ledger MUST record schema version `local_consumer_endpoint.ledger.v1`, immutable process launch id (`run_id`), a unique local `reservation_id` generated from at least 128 bits of CSPRNG input for every reservation, the same `run_id` and `reservation_id` copied onto every later state transition and audit row for that reservation, redacted request ids, model id, admission estimate or JSON null when `--no-budget` skips admission estimation, unpriced-override flag, no-budget flag when applicable, terminal local outcome, settled exposure amount when known, upstream request id when available, reservation state (`reserved`, `settled`, `held`, `released`, or `estimate_exceeded`), and created/updated timestamps; it MUST NOT record raw prompts, raw completions, bearer tokens, local bearer tokens, raw receipts, full upstream error bodies, hostnames, OS usernames, hardware serials, MAC addresses, or stable hardware UUIDs. A budgeted admission reservation MUST NOT be considered committed and MUST NOT be forwarded upstream until the ledger reservation append is durable; durable means the append bytes and required file metadata have been flushed with `fsync()` or a platform-equivalent durability primitive on the ledger file descriptor, and any newly created parent directory entry has been flushed with a platform-equivalent directory sync where supported. Every ledger state-transition append, including settlement, `estimate_exceeded`, held, released, and recovery audit entries, MUST satisfy the same durability rule before any local HTTP response, status output, recovery-command output, remaining-budget value, or restart-recovery decision relies on that transition. If a durable append fails, including fsync failure, the implementation MUST roll back any affected in-process reservation state when possible, mark ledger health unhealthy, return `local_budget_ledger_unavailable` for runtime chargeable paths, fail recovery commands nonzero without claiming success, and stop accepting chargeable requests until ledger health is restored. After a terminal upstream response, the ledger MUST settle a reservation to trusted upstream usage/cost evidence when such evidence is available, even when that evidence exceeds the admission estimate; if trusted usage/cost evidence is unavailable, it MUST settle to the admission estimate rather than inventing a lower cost. If trusted upstream usage/cost evidence exceeds the admission estimate, the ledger MUST record state `estimate_exceeded`, remaining budget MUST be allowed to reach zero or a negative value, status MUST surface the pricing-invariant breach, and the process MUST stop accepting new chargeable admission requests until restarted with corrected trusted pricing metadata or an explicit operator recovery path defined by a later spec; in-flight requests that already passed admission before `estimate_exceeded` was set MUST be allowed to complete. SPEC-005 billing and settlement remain authoritative. If the local client disconnects during streaming before trusted terminal usage/cost evidence is available, the implementation MUST cancel or close the upstream request when possible, wait no longer than one second for synchronous cancellation acknowledgement, and settle the reservation to the admission estimate unless the upstream returns trusted partial usage/cost evidence bound to the request. In-flight reservations MUST be treated conservatively on process restart: they become `held` and reduce remaining budget until a recovery command updates them. On graceful shutdown, including SIGTERM, the process MUST stop accepting new requests, drain in-flight requests for a bounded period no longer than five seconds, settle terminal requests, cancel or close remaining upstream requests, mark remaining in-flight reservations `held`, remove the active endpoint descriptor when possible, and then exit. Operators should expect long-running streaming requests that exceed the five-second drain bound to become held reservations requiring recovery-command handling; that operational cost is intentional in v0.1 because bounded shutdown takes precedence over waiting indefinitely. R005 conformance REQUIRES local recovery commands named `malibu-cli consume budget status` and `malibu-cli consume budget release-held`; `status` MUST show redacted held reservations, age, estimate, and ledger path class, while `release-held` MUST require a ledger selector `--ledger <path>` or `--ledger default`, a run selector `--run-id <process-launch-id>`, and `--confirm-release-held`, MUST fail rather than modify the ledger while another process holds the ledger lock, MUST only release held local reservations whose immutable `run_id` exactly matches that selected run, MUST append a redacted audit entry carrying the same `run_id` and each released `reservation_id`, MUST leave wrong-run and missing-reservation rows unchanged, and MUST NOT alter settled local exposure or upstream gateway records. `--ledger default` on recovery commands MUST resolve to the macOS default path computed at recovery-command invocation time from the invoking user's `$HOME`. Manual ledger deletion is not a conformant recovery path. If the ledger cannot be opened, locked, parsed, or written, budgeted mode MUST refuse to start or MUST stop accepting chargeable requests.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:145:R005 reservation state transitions are closed for v0.1: `reserved` MAY transition only to `settled`, `held`, or `estimate_exceeded`; `held` MAY transition only to `released` through `release-held`, or to `settled` only if trusted upstream terminal evidence bound to that reservation arrives before shutdown completion; `settled`, `released`, and `estimate_exceeded` are terminal for that reservation and MUST NOT transition to any other state. A recovery command MUST fail nonzero rather than appending a transition that violates this table. The ledger reservation state `estimate_exceeded` is per-reservation, while the R006 pricing trust state `estimate_exceeded` is process-level. When a reservation in the current process durably transitions to ledger state `estimate_exceeded`, the process MUST set status pricing trust state to `estimate_exceeded` and stop new chargeable admissions under R005/R006.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:157:**SPEC-045-R007 - Gateway error preservation and local error codes.** Upstream SPEC-006 errors and any syntactically valid upstream HTTP response, regardless of status code, MUST be proxied to the same local client under the preservation rule rather than being converted into local success or `local_upstream_unavailable`; `local_upstream_unavailable` applies only to transport failures and protocol-invalid responses. The local endpoint MAY return the upstream error body to the same local client that initiated the request, but logs, status, ledger rows, diagnostics, and other clients MUST receive only redacted error code/class/request-id material. Startup failures MUST return process exit codes and stderr error codes, not HTTP envelopes. Local-only HTTP failures MUST use an OpenAI-shaped error envelope with `error.type`, `error.message`, nullable `error.param`, `error.code`, and an extension object `error.macprovider` containing boolean `forwarded_upstream`, except `HEAD` responses MUST have an empty body regardless of error code. Local HTTP error codes MUST map as follows: `local_auth_required` to 401, `local_credential_missing` to 401, `local_invalid_request` to 400, `local_content_encoding_unsupported` to 415, `local_model_not_allowed` to 400, `local_pricing_unavailable` to 503, `local_budget_required` to 400, `local_request_too_large` to 413, `local_endpoint_busy` to 503, `local_budget_exceeded` to 402, `local_budget_ledger_unavailable` to 503, `local_estimate_exceeded` to 503, `local_endpoint_unsupported` to 404 or 405 as appropriate for the path/method, and `local_upstream_unavailable` to 502 when the upstream returns an unparseable or protocol-invalid response, closes before returning response headers, or returns response headers for a non-streaming response but the body is truncated by reset or EOF before any local response body bytes are sent, and to 503 when the upstream is unreachable or times out before returning response headers. Once a streaming `text/event-stream` response has sent local response headers or body bytes, the implementation MUST NOT attempt to change the HTTP status to 502; on upstream reset, EOF, or protocol-invalid truncation after that point it MUST emit a terminal SSE error event carrying redacted `local_upstream_unavailable` code material when the local connection is still writable, then close the stream and settle the ledger conservatively under R005. `local_bind_rejected`, `local_credential_flag_rejected`, `local_budget_flag_rejected`, `local_upstream_url_rejected`, and `local_active_endpoint_exists` are reserved only for startup failure and MUST NOT be returned by a running HTTP server. Local response headers forwarded from the upstream gateway MUST be allowlisted to OpenAI/SPEC-006 compatibility metadata: content type, upstream `Content-Encoding` when body bytes remain encoded, upstream `Cache-Control`, rate-limit and retry headers, request id, receipt header, streaming-mode header, and other explicitly named `X-MacProvider-*` response metadata defined by SPEC-006, SPEC-015, SPEC-018, or a later dependency; the local warning header `X-MacProvider-Warning` MAY be added by SPEC-045. `Content-Encoding` MUST accompany the upstream body bytes verbatim when forwarded. `Cache-Control` MUST be forwarded only when received from upstream, and the local proxy MUST NOT add a permissive cache policy locally. Local errors MUST identify whether the request was forwarded upstream through `error.macprovider.forwarded_upstream`; local-only errors set it to `false`, and locally generated upstream-transport errors set it to `true` only after request bytes were sent upstream. The same `local_upstream_unavailable` code may appear with either `forwarded_upstream` value depending on whether the transport failure occurred before or after request bytes were sent upstream. The implementation MUST NOT retry non-idempotent chat completions after bytes have been sent upstream unless the gateway supplies an idempotency contract and the request is bound to it; before bytes are sent, it MAY perform at most one bounded connection attempt per upstream request before returning `local_upstream_unavailable`.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:161:`local_request_cap_exceeded` MUST map to HTTP 402 and MUST be local-only with `error.macprovider.forwarded_upstream=false`. Upstream 3xx responses are intentionally returned without `Location` when preserved under R003/R007; this fail-closed protocol deviation prevents redirect-target credential exfiltration and implementations MUST NOT synthesize an alternate redirect target.
phase3-binary/Sources/macprovider-cli/Build1LaneAArtifactStager.swift:55:/// Invariants preserved on every exit path:
phase3-binary/Sources/macprovider-cli/Build1LaneAArtifactStager.swift:67:    /// SPEC-044 preparation reserve: `available >= 2 * estimated_bytes + 1 GiB`
specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:52:- SPEC-002 owns provider assignment, capacity, request lifecycle, cancellation, and coordinator `request_log`. SPEC-041 adds binding and state constraints without bypassing those owners.
specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:140:Public and coordinator buyer-port `POST /v1/relay-blind/route-reservations` preserve the existing closed request schema exactly: `endpoint_family`, `model`, `stream`, `max_output_tokens`, `input_token_upper_bound`, and `encrypted_request_bytes`. It rejects duplicate, unknown, null, trailing, malformed, noncanonical, overflowed, or out-of-bound fields before state creation. The route is mounted even when disabled so valid requests receive typed `relay_blind_disabled`, never an untyped 404. Every response sets `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`. The public route uses the eventual request's normal API-key or signed wallet-session authentication. Pool selection is not a body field. Any nonempty pool-selection header or other authenticated pool intent is rejected before reservation, quota, or dispatch under SPEC-042-R009. The gateway forwards closed metadata with existing trusted gateway Authorization and trusted account/session context. The coordinator rejects non-gateway callers.
specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:144:Reservation binds immutably to the authenticated account/session, live provider ID and assigned session, signed record digest and `kid`, canonical and provider models, endpoint, stream, all caps, byte bound, and explicit empty pool selection. Key discovery does not reserve capacity or quota. Existing provider capacity is acquired only at dispatch.
specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:148:Recovery uses authenticated internal `POST /v1/relay-blind/status` with exactly `provider_binding_digest` and `envelope_digest`, each canonical base64url SHA-256. The closed response contains `version: relay-blind-status-v1`, `state`, `internal_request_id`, `validated`, nullable `input_tokens`, nullable `completion_tokens`, `effective_privacy_outcome`, and `retry_action: do_not_resubmit`. Input is present exactly when authenticated usage is known; completion is present only for `terminal`. This endpoint never dispatches. It atomically fences expired `reserved` or `consumed_predispatch` rows to `rejected` before reporting them; fresh rows remain held to avoid a concurrent dispatch/refund race. `unknown_postdispatch` is irreversible and settles known input and locally recorded delivered output only. Usage knowledge and satisfied privacy are independent facts.
specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:152:The atomic state machine is `available -> consumed -> dispatched -> terminal`. Only an exact authenticated envelope may conditionally change `available` to `consumed`; the transition happens before quota or dispatch. Quota failure, disabled/unavailable outcome, expiry, denial, and applicable terminal rejection burn the reservation/envelope and never restore `available`. The coordinator arms dispatch exactly once after revalidation and capacity/quota admission. Duplicate, uncertain, or recovered dispatched work MUST NOT dispatch again. Indexed expiry, row/byte/rate ceilings, and bounded sanitized audits prevent rejection-state amplification. Persistent store error or unknown freshness disables availability.
specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:154:Gateway replay state remains durable across restart and configuration cycling and is checked before rate/capacity classification. Applicable single-use material is durably recorded before disabled/unavailable rejection, so a later configuration change cannot revive it. Coordinator consumption and dispatch state independently prevent duplicate dispatch. There is no network retry of consume or dispatch; uncertainty fails closed.
specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:156:The acceptance state names are fixed. Coordinator owns `reserved -> consumed_predispatch -> dispatched -> terminal`, with `rejected` and `unknown_postdispatch` terminal fences. Provider owns `claimed -> validated -> terminal`; a restarted `claimed` or `validated` entry becomes `unknown_postdispatch` and never reexecutes. Gateway owns `quota_held` followed by the existing settled/refunded/pending journal states. Reservation or `consumed_predispatch` alone never permits billing. Cancel, timeout, key/session staleness, or component restart before dispatch burns material, refunds held quota, and returns `new_reservation_and_envelope` when otherwise retryable. After dispatch, cancel, timeout, disconnect, restart uncertainty, or terminal-evidence loss becomes `unknown_postdispatch`, never resubmits, and bills only known usage/delivered output through existing recovery with `do_not_resubmit`. Provider terminal-evidence loss preserves the durable terminal claim while coordinator/gateway reconcile accounting. Tests cover every transition/crash cut and duplicate settlement delivery.
specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:170:Journal error, capacity exhaustion, or uncertain recovery fails closed. A claimed or uncertain entry after restart always rejects duplicate execution. Crash before claim may be retried only through the same coordinator recovery decision without creating new envelope material; crash after claim, after decrypt, after first token, or during terminal persistence MUST NOT execute again.
specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:180:Relay-blind work uses existing quota, SPEC-005 settlement, gateway `usage_events`/journal, and coordinator `request_log`; there is no parallel ledger. Existing records gain bounded additive facts: `requested_privacy_mode`, `effective_privacy_outcome`, `relay_blind_envelope_digest`, `relay_blind_key_record_digest`, `relay_blind_kid`, `relay_blind_provider_binding_digest`, durable clear caps, and an explicit positive-receipt/reward exclusion. Existing default values mean plaintext. Recovery preserves the same caps/outcome and at most one settlement.
specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:210:Required mode fails closed before quota when unavailable. No generic 503 helper may replay a reservation, consume call, dispatch call, or ciphertext. A retryable result authorizes only a wholly new reservation, ephemeral key, nonce, request identifier, and envelope. Replay classification takes precedence over rate/capacity classification. Any `relay-blind-request-*` namespace is relay-shaped and can never enter plaintext parsing. Any mode other than `required`, provider/key substitution, HTTP fallback, cross-provider failover, altered model/caps, or plaintext conversion is `relay_blind_downgrade_rejected`.
